observations: Torah #100 is a short teaching about hitbodedut as the essential practice for becoming a true ish kasher. While several concepts are mentioned (hitbodedut, ish kasher, tzaddikim, David HaMelech, Sefer Tehillim, zera haBaal Shem Tov), no bechina language is used anywhere in the text. All relationships are eitza-type (cause-and-effect): hitbodedut leads to becoming kasher, David's practice produced Tehillim, etc. Without bechina connections, no packages can be formed. The torah is an eitza teaching — practical advice about the centrality of hitbodedut — rather than a conceptual-mapping torah that identifies parallel aspects.
